finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.untrusted_source: The size of the buffer 'path' is determined by the return value of _NSGetExecutablePath, which can be larger than the initially allocated size.
finding.trigger: If the path to the current executable is longer than 1024 characters, _NSGetExecutablePath will return a non-zero value, and the buffer 'path' will not be properly initialized.
finding.assumptions: The function _NSGetExecutablePath can return a path longer than the initially allocated buffer size, and the buffer 'path' is not re-allocated or resized based on the returned size.

parsed.change_summary: Added a reallocation of the buffer if the initial size is insufficient to hold the executable path.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the code now checks if the initial buffer is too small and reallocates it with the required size before attempting to print the executable path again.
parsed.behavior_changes: The behavior has changed in that the program now attempts to reallocate the buffer if the initial size is insufficient and tries to get the executable path again. If the reallocation fails, it prints an error message.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Checked the behavior of _NSGetExecutablePath: it writes at most *bufsize bytes and returns non‑zero if the buffer is too small, leaving the buffer unchanged. 2) Verified that the code only calls printf with 'path' when the function returns 0 (line 10), i.e., when the buffer was successfully filled. 3) Confirmed that when the function fails (lines 12‑13) the buffer is not used, so no overflow can occur.
